payload.reason: The evidence provides specific performance metrics comparing the SubGram model to the Skip-gram model, indicating the gains achieved by the SubGram model.

claims.text: The SubGram model significantly outperforms the Skip-gram model on the same training set, achieving 22.4% compared to Skip-gram's 9.7%.
The performance of the SubGram model on the original test set is similar to that of the Skip-gram model, with scores of 42.5% and 42.3% respectively.
The Skip-gram model trained on a larger dataset achieves a performance of 43.5%, indicating potential for further improvement of the SubGram model with more data.
